# Typography

> Heading and Text over the token-driven type scale: level is the document outline, size is the rung, tone is the color role, className stays layout-only. TextLink is the underlined link inside prose. A bare text-* rung is for HTML React doesn't render as components, such as email HTML; MDX maps its tags to Heading and Text.

This file matches the installed `typography` source. The online docs follow the latest release and may describe a newer version.

## Install

```bash
npx shadcn@latest add https://control-ui.dev/r/typography.json
```

With `@ctrl-ui/react` instead of the registry, import from `@ctrl-ui/react/` where this file says `@/components/control-ui/`; this file then lives at `node_modules/@ctrl-ui/react/dist/docs/typography.md`.

- `@/components/control-ui/ui/typography`: `headingClassName`, `Heading`, `Text`, `TextLink`, types `TypeSize`, `TypeTone`, `TextWeight`, `HeadingLevel`, `HeadingProps`, `TextTag`, `TextProps`, `TextLinkProps`

## Composition

### Heading and Text

Heading takes level (the document outline) and size (the rung); they are decoupled on purpose, so an h3 may wear heading-2. Text takes as, size, weight, and tone. className is for layout only: size, weight, face, and color come from props.

```tsx
page section
  <Heading />
  <Text />
```

### Inline link

TextLink styles one link inside running text and stays inline so it wraps with the sentence. Pass render={<Link />} to keep your router.

```tsx
<Text>
  <TextLink />
</Text>
```

### Native tag

A native tag may wear one text-* rung and nothing else from the scale: pair it with a tone or weight and it becomes Text or Heading. Heading rungs already carry font-display and text-balance.

```tsx
one rung on the element
  <h2 />
  <p />
```

## Usage

```tsx
"use client";

import { Heading, Text, TextLink } from "@/components/control-ui/ui/typography";

export function TypographyTokensExample() {
  return (
    <div className="flex w-full max-w-2xl flex-col gap-6">
      <Text as="p" size="hero">
        Hero — fluid landing headlines
      </Text>
      <Text as="p" size="display">
        Display — page titles &amp; heroes
      </Text>
      <Heading level={1}>Heading 1 — content h1</Heading>
      <Heading level={2}>One rung per size, named by role</Heading>
      <Heading level={3}>Level picks the tag, size defaults to the matching rung</Heading>
      <Heading level={4}>One class per heading: face, weight, and balance ride along</Heading>
      <Heading level={3} size="heading-2" tone="muted">
        An h3 wearing heading-2: level is the outline, size is the look
      </Heading>
      <Text as="p" size="body-lg">
        Body large sets the emphasized reading size — intros, lead paragraphs, and anywhere copy needs a little more presence than the
        default.
      </Text>
      <Text as="p">
        Body is the default for paragraphs, controls, and most of the interface. The five boxing wizards jump quickly, and the quick brown
        fox jumps over the lazy dog.
      </Text>
      <Text as="p">
        Weight: <Text weight="normal">normal</Text>, <Text weight="medium">medium</Text>, <Text weight="semibold">semibold</Text>,{" "}
        <Text weight="bold">bold</Text> for figures and overlays that must read at a glance.
      </Text>
      <Text as="p" tone="muted">
        A <TextLink href="#typography">text link</TextLink> sits inside prose: it inherits the size and stays underlined at rest.
      </Text>
      <Text as="p" size="label" tone="muted">
        Label — form labels and small chrome.
      </Text>
      <Text as="p" size="caption" tone="muted">
        Caption — overlines, timestamps, and group labels.
      </Text>
      <Text as="p" size="micro" tone="muted">
        Micro — keycaps, badge counters, and dense metadata.
      </Text>
    </div>
  );
}
```
